title: Tariqs list of bot builds
subtitle: His list, batched. Nothing reworded, nothing merged, nothing dropped.
howToRead: Every item below has a permanent id, B01 to B43, in the order you typed them. The id never changes. If the list is re-sorted or something is added in the middle, B14 is still B14.

Section 1 is your list, word for word, in your order. Section 2 is the same 43 items sorted into batches of similar work, each one appearing once, called up by id. Section 3 is the eight agent version ChatGPT wrote for you.

Nothing in section 1 has been edited. A script checks that every paragraph you typed is still in this file, word for word, in the same order, and it will not let the file be saved if one is missing. Your typos are left exactly as you typed them.

Two ways to add to it, both fine. Type it yourself on one of the blank numbered lines at the end of section 1 and save: Word gives it the next id. Or tell the agent: add to my bot list, then what you want, and it writes it in for you and asks you to approve the save. It will not overwrite a change you made yourself.
Either way the new item is in your list straight away. It will not be sorted into a batch in section 2 until Jaiah files it, because which batch it belongs in is a decision, not a guess.
crossRefNote: Five items point at another item. Three are clear. Two name a number that does not match what the sentence is about, so both readings are shown and neither has been corrected. They are marked below for you to settle.
_catchAllNote: His list is the source of truth and the batched document derives from it, so an item he adds is in section 1 straight away but belongs to no batch until a person decides which one. It lands here rather than being dropped or guessed at. Move the id into a real batch above when it is decided.

catchAll.title: Batch 14. Added since, not yet batched
catchAll.what: Items added to the list after the batches were drawn up. They are in your list and they are not lost; nobody has decided which batch they belong in yet.

batches.title: Batch 1. Files, notes and tasks
batches.what: The job that files a document where it belongs and turns what you said into a task.
batches.needs: OneDrive is connected. Monday.com needs an API token from you or Kendal.

batches.title: Batch 2. The daily rhythm: morning brief and afternoon close out
batches.what: One job that runs twice a day and tells you what is coming and what did not happen.
batches.needs: Mail and your diary are connected. Staff calendars and a second to do calendar need the read app finished. The TV is a page on the dashboard you already have.

batches.title: Batch 3. Email and messages as one layer
batches.what: Everything that arrives, read for you, grouped, answered in your words or quarantined.
batches.needs: Reading and drafting work now. Sending, forwarding and deleting need Mail.Send and Mail.ReadWrite. Teams and WhatsApp come after.

batches.title: Batch 4. Staff: performance, reviews and touch points
batches.what: Every person on a register with their dates, so the reminders and the chasing happen on their own.
batches.needs: A staff register with start dates and review dates. MYOB payroll or a sheet Kendal keeps. B04 is activity monitoring and needs its own decision before it is built.

batches.title: Batch 5. Marketing: posts and video
batches.what: Posting and content, planned a week ahead, from footage you dump.
batches.needs: Posting access to the Instagram and Facebook business accounts, and one folder you drop footage into.

batches.title: Batch 6. Winning work: estimating, tenders and blasts
batches.what: Finding the work, pricing it, and chasing the prices that have not come back.
batches.needs: Mail.Send, the OneDrive path of the TFA tender template, and one place the tender register lives.

batches.title: Batch 7. The TFA book: contacts, subbies and the build method
batches.what: TFA's own knowledge written down once, so every other agent can read it instead of guessing.
batches.needs: A decision on where the register lives, and your hold points captured once. This is the shared knowledge base you asked for in section 3.

batches.title: Batch 8. Advisers: legal, accounting and QBCC
batches.what: A first pass on a legal or tax question, with what to confirm with the real adviser marked.
batches.needs: Nothing new to connect. It needs a fixed structure so the answer is the same shape every time, and the documents readable from OneDrive.

batches.title: Batch 9. Think like Tariq: ideas, ventures and the protocol
batches.what: Throw it a half formed idea and get back a structured read on it, judged the way you judge things.
batches.needs: Your commercial principles written down so it can argue back. Web search already works.

batches.title: Batch 10. Land and sites
batches.what: Watching for land and development sites that match what you are after.
batches.needs: A source. realestate.com.au has no public feed, so this is the browser lane on an allowed site, or a paid data source.

batches.title: Batch 11. Launching a brand: websites, Shopify and registration
batches.what: Taking a brand from idea to a site, a store and a registered entity.
batches.needs: A Shopify store and key when there is something to sell. Site builds are a separate piece of work, not this agent.

batches.title: Batch 12. Personal: buying, accounts and health
batches.what: Your own side. Finding things, watching for deals, keeping logins somewhere proper, health in one place.
batches.needs: A password manager on the mini, not notes. Buying stays off until you set the approval limits. Health needs whichever app you already use.

batches.title: Batch 13. The front door
batches.what: How you reach it and how the next agent gets decided.
batches.needs: Telegram is the front door today and it works. A separate mobile number is a second one if you want it.

chatgpt.label: Section 3. His ChatGPT version
intro: This is not Tariq's typing. It is the eight agent rewrite ChatGPT made of the same list, pasted into his email of 11 Sep 2026. It is here because it is a useful second view of the same 43 items, and because the system wide requirements at the end are things he asked for that are not items on the list.
Reproduced from docs/tariq-agent-roadmap-2026-09-11.md. The build status notes that sit alongside each agent in that file are left out here; read the file itself for where each one stands today.
chatgpt.objective: Overall objective, his: an AI operating system around Tariq that reduces administration, prevents things being forgotten, gives visibility across TFA, responds to repetitive matters, assists decision-making and progressively takes actions on his behalf. Monday.com stays the primary operational task source; the AI sits above all systems.

agents.title: 1. Executive Command Centre, "Run My Day"
agents.body: Captures email, calendar, Monday.com, Teams, messages, call notes and documents and works out what needs action. Files documents to the right project. Turns commitments into tasks and allocates them through Monday.com. Morning executive brief (meetings, staff meetings, overdue, outstanding responses, project issues, decisions needed) and an afternoon close-out. A separate AI to-do / time-blocking calendar that does not touch the real one. Time analysis with recommendations. A live dashboard on the TV in his office.

agents.title: 2. Communications Agent, "Tariq Inbox"
agents.body: One layer over email and, where possible, Teams, WhatsApp, SMS. Short versions, what needs action, related threads grouped, prior correspondence understood. One-touch replies in his voice, learning the register per audience (staff, consultants, lawyers, clients, mates, suppliers). Auto-forward rules (Accor Plus to Ziana) he can add to. Low-value mail into a daily quarantine report, with "never show me this again" rules he approves. Routine staff questions answered automatically from prior mail, records and policies; technical, contractual, unusual or commercially sensitive escalated. Call notes into a simple personal CRM so promises and follow-ups from calls are captured.

agents.title: 3. People and Performance, "TFA People"
agents.body: Every employee: role, start date, probation, salary review dates, birthdays, KPIs, performance discussions, development objectives. Reminders with a drafted note for birthdays, probation reviews, 6-month catch-ups, annual reviews. Morning overview of staff calendars where relevant. A KPI dashboard from agreed objective measures. A short working-style questionnaire per staff member so he gets management cues before a meeting (from what they provide plus legitimate observations, not invented profiles). Computer activity monitoring only as a separate, transparent, compliance-approved module.

agents.title: 4. Estimating, Leads and Business Development, "Win Work"
agents.body: Tender packages for estimators with links and documents; estimator blasts; response tracking; automatic follow-up of outstanding pricing. An estimating agent that reviews drawings and specs, builds scopes, identifies trade packages, finds missing information, compares subcontractor quotes, produces estimate summaries and flags commercial risk, with human approval before any tender goes out. Lead, referral and follow-up tracking.

agents.title: 5. Development and Venture Studio, "Create"
agents.body: Throw an idea at it with nothing prepared; it returns a structured concept, gaps, feasibility, research, capital, revenue, margin, competitors, next steps and a verdict. A repeatable protocol for assessing businesses, products and development concepts. Learns his commercial principles (speed, margin, risk, execution difficulty, competitive advantage, self-perform, scalability, wealth creation) and challenges weak ideas. Finds development sites matching criteria; finds gaps in construction, technology, ecommerce; a roadmap to a $200m+ group.

agents.title: 6. Digital Business Launch, "Build and Launch"
agents.body: From concept to execution: competitor and adjacent-industry research, brand and website structure, new websites built from those lessons, Shopify products and listings, launch materials, and the admin steps to set up a business with accountant, lawyer, ASIC and human approvals flagged.

agents.title: 7. Personal Life and Commerce, "Tariq Personal"
agents.body: Research and source purchases (Marketplace, retail, Amazon), compare, recommend, negotiate where appropriate. Monitor things he is interested in (cars, equipment, deals) and alert him. Eventually purchasing under approval limits (one-touch below a threshold, explicit confirmation above). Never store passwords in notes or memory; integrate a proper password manager and request credentials securely. A personal fitness and health dashboard kept separate from TFA staff systems.

agents.title: 8. Professional Advisory, "Legal and Finance Copilots"
agents.body: Legal: property due diligence, conveyancing, construction contracts, disputes; review documents, identify risks, say what his lawyer should be doing, prepare questions, compare advice against documents, draft commercially strong correspondence. Not a replacement for specialist advice. Finance: entity, trust and property structures, tax consequences, payroll tax, incentives and training arrangements, EOFY planning, scenario modelling, with what needs the accountant's confirmation clearly marked.

systemWide: One shared, authorised TFA knowledge base, tagged by project, company, person, client and subject.

Approval hierarchy: Level 1 observe (no approval), Level 2 prepare for one-touch approval, Level 3 pre-approved routine actions, Level 4 sensitive actions always need Tariq (payments, contracts, legal submissions, employee decisions, major purchases, registrations, external commitments).
Audit trail for every autonomous action: what, why, what it relied on.
A "Tariq Rules / Decision Book": every correction becomes a durable rule.
Stronger controls on staff monitoring, legal and tax decisions, credentials and autonomous purchases.
